recipes.af: Reheat the sweet potato rounds at 175°C for 6–8 minutes and they crisp back up — this is what the source actually recommends.

veg.how: Second tray, same 230°C oven, for the last 20 minutes of the sweet potatoes. Pack them in beside the eggs.

recipes.name: High-Protein Breakfast Sausage Bowls

ing.n: sweet potatoes, sliced into ½" rounds
black pepper, red pepper flakes, smoked paprika, kosher salt

steps: Toss the sweet potato rounds with 2 Tbsp olive oil on a parchment-lined sheet pan in a single layer. Bake at 450°F / 230°C on the bottom rack for 40–45 minutes, until caramelised and browned. Salt immediately out of the oven.
While they roast, mix the sausage spices with the maple syrup and broth in one bowl, and whisk the eggs in another. Set both aside until the potatoes have about 15 minutes left.

Brown the ground turkey in ½ Tbsp olive oil over medium-high for 3–4 minutes, breaking it apart. Once cooked through, pour in the spice-and-syrup mixture and cook 2–3 minutes more until barely any liquid remains.
Scramble the eggs in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat with the remaining ½ Tbsp oil. Season with salt and pepper and pull them slightly underdone — they finish cooking on reheat.
Assemble each bowl: roughly 115 g sausage, 9 sweet potato slices, 85 g egg, ¼ cup cottage cheese, and one-sixth of the avocado.
recipes.store: Fridge 4–5 days; the sausage and potatoes freeze well. Reheat at 50% microwave power in 60-second bursts, or crisp the potatoes back under the grill for 3–4 minutes.
recipes.tune: Already inside your window at 650 kcal with 60 g protein — this is the single best macro profile in the collection. Cut the maple syrup to ¼ cup if you want it less sweet; it costs about 20 kcal a bowl.
recipes.flag: Assemble the avocado fresh rather than packing it — it browns over four days where everything else here holds fine.

recipes.af: From thawed: unwrap, spritz with oil, 200°C for 8–9 minutes, turning halfway. Far better shell than the microwave gives you.

veg.how: Cook the mushrooms and extra pepper with the onion until the pan is properly dry, then wilt the spinach in before the eggs go on. Dry veg is what keeps a freezer burrito from going soggy.

recipes.name: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
steps: Shred the cheese; dice the onion and bell pepper. Sauté the vegetables in ½ Tbsp butter until the onion turns translucent, season, and tip into a bowl.
Dice the ham and brown it in another ½ Tbsp butter. Move to a separate bowl and wipe the skillet.
Whisk the eggs. Melt the last 1 Tbsp butter and scramble over medium heat until mostly set but still moist — stop early, they cook again on reheat. Season.
Lay out the tortillas and divide the eggs, vegetables, cheese and ham between them.
Roll each one: fold the bottom up over the filling, fold both sides in, then finish the roll.
Wrap each burrito in parchment using the same folds, label, and stack in freezer bags.
recipes.store: Freezer up to 3 months. From thawed: 1–2 minutes in the microwave, or 5 minutes a side in a dry skillet for a crisp shell. From frozen: 5 minutes on defrost, then 1–2 minutes on high.
recipes.tune: At 421 kcal it's a light breakfast. Two burritos is 842 kcal and 56 g protein — too much; one burrito plus a 170 g pot of Greek yoghurt lands at 545 kcal / 45 g protein, which is exactly right.
recipes.flag: 1,275 mg sodium per burrito, mostly from the ham and tortilla. If you're eating these daily, swap the ham for cooked ground turkey or chicken sausage and it roughly halves.

veg.how: Soften the pepper with the sausage, stir the extra spinach into the eggs, and dot the halved tomatoes over the top before it goes into the oven.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese, Egg & Sausage Frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C with a rack in the second-highest position. Lightly spray a 10-inch oven-safe skillet.
Whisk the eggs, cottage cheese, Pecorino, spinach, salt and pepper together in a bowl and set aside.
Break the sausage into small pieces in the skillet over medium heat and cook until browned through, about 4 minutes.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and cook 1 minute, just to set the bottom.
Bake 16–18 minutes, until the top is set.
Slide the frittata onto a board and cut into 4 wedges.
recipes.store: Wedges keep 3–4 days in the fridge. Bring to room temperature or microwave in 30-second bursts.
recipes.tune: 233 kcal is a component, not a meal. A wedge with two slices of wholemeal toast and butter is 520 kcal / 30 g protein / 8 g fibre. Two wedges plus one slice gets you to 640 kcal / 48 g protein.

veg.how: Stir fresh raspberries in the night before, or scatter them on in the morning. Highest-fibre fruit there is.

fz.how: Drop them in frozen with everything else — they thaw overnight and bleed into the oats.

recipes.name: High-Protein Overnight Oats

ing.n: vanilla or chocolate protein powder (whey–casein blend)

steps: Put everything in a jar or sealable container.
Shake hard until the protein powder is fully dispersed — this is the step people skip and then find clumps.
Refrigerate overnight.
Stir and eat cold. Add crunchy toppings the morning of, not the night before.
recipes.store: Up to 5 days in sealed jars — build five on Sunday and breakfast is done for the week.
recipes.tune: Add 1 Tbsp peanut butter (+95 kcal, +4 g protein) and a sliced banana (+105 kcal, +3 g fibre) and the jar hits about 630 kcal / 45 g protein / 9 g fibre.
recipes.flag: Built with ordinary milk rather than the almond milk the source uses, which is why these macros are higher than the published 359 kcal — semi-skimmed adds roughly 70 kcal, 5 g protein and 7 g carbs per jar. Whole milk adds about 30 kcal more again. It's the one recipe here with no meat, and the one to make when you have a 7am start.

veg.how: Pack 100 g beside the pancakes. Fresh raspberries only keep 2–3 days, so they're the thing to buy closest to cook day.

fz.how: Pack 100 g frozen in the box beside the pancakes; they're thawed by breakfast. Or a minute in the microwave for a warm sauce.

recipes.name: Blender Cottage Cheese Protein Pancakes

ing.n: cottage cheese, full fat blends smoothest
butter, oil or spray for the pan

ing.s: Your version — see the note below

ing.n: milk, to loosen the batter back out

steps: Put everything in a high-speed blender in the order listed and blend about 30 seconds, until smooth. Don't over-blend — the oats going gluey is what makes rubbery pancakes.
Let the batter sit 5 minutes. This is the step that matters: the oats hydrate and the batter thickens, and skipping it gives you thin, floppy pancakes.
Heat a large non-stick skillet or griddle over low-to-medium heat and add your cooking fat. Low and slow — a hot pan burns the outside before the middle sets.
Pour about ¼ cup of batter per pancake and shape them into even rounds.
Cook 3–4 minutes, until the batter has clearly set at the edges, then flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days, freezer 3 months. Freeze them flat on parchment first, then bag them — a frozen pancake goes straight in the toaster, which is the whole point.
recipes.tune: Adding your usual scoop of protein powder puts one serving at roughly 513 kcal / 49 g protein — but protein powder soaks up liquid, so add 2–4 Tbsp of milk or the batter turns to paste. Two servings' worth (all six pancakes) with a sliced banana is about 620 kcal and 52 g protein.
recipes.flag: This version gets its 25 g protein from the cottage cheese and eggs alone — no powder. If you'd rather swap the oats for pancake mix, use about 90 g of mix and drop the baking powder, since the mix already has raising agent in it; expect roughly the same calories with 4–5 g less fibre.

veg.how: 50 g into each jar with the mango and blueberries.

fz.how: 50 g frozen into each jar — they thaw by morning and loosen the yoghurt slightly.

recipes.name: Yoghurt, Granola & Fruit Jars
steps: Layer the yoghurt and fruit into four jars: 1 cup yoghurt, ¼ cup mango and ¼ cup blueberries each.
Put the granola in a separate small container or bag — 24 g per jar. Do not layer it in.
Refrigerate. Tip the granola in the moment you eat it.
recipes.store: Jars keep 4–5 days. Granola lives in the cupboard, not the fridge.
recipes.tune: Two scoops (60 g) of granola instead of one plus a tablespoon of peanut butter takes a jar to about 545 kcal / 28 g protein. Or stir a half-scoop of protein powder through the yoghurt: +60 kcal, +12 g protein, no change in volume.
recipes.flag: The source publishes no nutrition, so these macros are my calculation from the gram weights listed, using standard values for vanilla non-fat Greek yoghurt and a typical granola. Your granola is the swing factor — they run from 380 to 500 kcal per 100 g, so check the packet and adjust.

veg.how: Onto the pepper tray for the last 15 minutes — same oven, same temperature.

recipes.name: Salsa Chicken Meal Prep Bowls
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Rinse the basmati until the water runs clear, then put it in a covered pot with the salt and water, bring to the boil, drop to low and simmer 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered another 10 minutes before fluffing.
Put the chicken breasts in a medium saucepan with the salsa, broth and chilli powder and stir briefly.
Cover, bring to the boil on high, then reduce to low and simmer 30 minutes at a steady simmer.
Cut the peppers into ½-inch strips, spread on a baking sheet, drizzle with oil, toss and salt.
Roast 20–25 minutes until browned at the edges, stirring once halfway.
Lift the chicken onto a board, shred with two forks, and return it to the salsa.
Into each container: about ¾ cup rice, a quarter of the peppers, a quarter of the chicken, and a spoonful of the salsa liquid.
Top with spring onion and a dollop of sour cream. Keeps 4 days.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 4 days. Microwave 2–3 minutes; add the sour cream after heating rather than before.
recipes.tune: Add 130 g cooked rice (+170 kcal) and it clears 620 kcal. Or keep the rice and add ½ an avocado (+160 kcal, +5 g fibre) for 615 kcal with better fats.
recipes.flag: Swapped to basmati: the fibre above is down from the source's 6 g to 4 g, and the rice cooks in 12 minutes instead of 35. Separately, 1,348 mg sodium — the jarred salsa is doing that; a no-salt-added salsa drops it by roughly a third with no real change in flavour.

recipes.af: Do the potatoes in the air fryer at 200°C for 15–18 minutes instead of the oven, and cook the chicken on the hob at the same time — halves the wall-clock time.

veg.how: On the broccoli tray, but in 10 minutes before the broccoli — carrots take longer.

recipes.name: Parmesan Potato & Ranch Chicken Prep
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Wash and dice the potatoes into ¾-inch pieces.
Mix the Parmesan, garlic powder, paprika and salt, then toss it through the potatoes with 1 Tbsp oil.
Spread the potatoes on a parchment-lined baking sheet and roast 30 minutes, until golden.
Toss the broccoli with oil, salt and pepper and spread on a second sheet.
Roast the broccoli about 20 minutes, until browned at the edges.
Butterfly the chicken breasts into thinner fillets and season with the garlic-herb blend.
Heat a large skillet over medium, add 1 Tbsp oil, and cook the chicken 5–6 minutes a side.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes on a board, then slice into strips.
Divide potatoes, broccoli and chicken between four containers with 2 Tbsp ranch each.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Keep the ranch in a separate pot and add it cold after reheating — heated ranch splits.
recipes.tune: The published 486 kcal excludes the dressing; 2 Tbsp ranch adds about 130 kcal, so as-packed you're at roughly 615 kcal. That's already in your window — no top-up needed.
recipes.flag: 8 g fibre a box, the best of the chicken recipes, thanks to the skin-on potato and a full 450 g of broccoli.

veg.how: Into the steak pan for 3–4 minutes once the steak comes out, with a splash of water and the lid on. Or microwave-steam, 4–5 minutes.

fz.how: Microwave-steam from frozen: covered bowl, 3 Tbsp water, 7–8 minutes, stir halfway.

recipes.name: Chipotle Steak & Pepper Bowls

ing.n: chilli powder, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper
baking soda — this is the tenderiser, don't skip it
basmati rice, uncooked (yields about 600 g cooked)
bell peppers, one green one red

steps: Cook the rice the day before if you can — day-old rice dries out slightly and fries far better.
Firm the steak in the freezer for a couple of hours; it makes thin slicing possible.
Mix 1 Tbsp oil, 1 Tbsp soy sauce, all the seasonings and the baking soda into a marinade.
Slice the steak thin (¼ inch) against the grain, then dice into small pieces. Massage the marinade in and leave 30–60 minutes.
Dice the peppers, slice the onion thin, mince the garlic, and mince 3 Tbsp of chipotle in adobo.
Cook the steak in a hot skillet in two batches with ½ Tbsp oil each — undisturbed 2 minutes, flip, 2 minutes more. Set aside.
Add 2 tsp oil with the onion and peppers, cook 2–3 minutes. Add the corn and garlic for 1–2 minutes.
Push everything to the sides, add the rice, soy sauce, lime juice and chipotle into the middle, and stir to break the rice up.
Return the steak, stir through, and adjust the salt. Divide evenly between five containers.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 5 days — one of the better keepers here, because the rice is fried rather than steamed.
recipes.tune: Add 100 g cooked rice (+130 kcal) or 60 g extra steak (+110 kcal, +18 g protein) to reach 610–630 kcal.
recipes.flag: The baking soda in the marinade is a velveting trick: it raises the surface pH so a cheap round steak stays tender in a hot pan. Rinse nothing off — half a teaspoon across 680 g is imperceptible.

veg.how: Into the beef pan for the last 3 minutes of the simmer, lid on — it steams in the sauce and picks up the flavour. No second pan.

fz.how: Microwave-steam from frozen, covered, 6–7 minutes. Drizzle some of the beef sauce over it in the box.

recipes.name: Korean Beef Rice Bowls

ing.n: basmati rice, uncooked (makes the 3 cups cooked)

steps: Combine the soy sauce, 2 Tbsp water, brown sugar, sesame oil and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Heat a large non-stick skillet on high, spray with oil, add the beef and cook about 5 minutes, breaking it up as it browns.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Pour the sauce over the beef, cover, and simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Build each bowl with ¾ cup rice, a scant ⅔ cup beef, cucumber, gochujang, sesame seeds and spring onion.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Pack the cucumber separately — it weeps if it sits in the sauce. 30 minutes start to finish makes this the one to cook on a weeknight when Sunday's prep ran out.
recipes.tune: The lightest main here. Add 150 g cooked rice (+195 kcal) and a fried egg (+90 kcal, +6 g protein) for 680 kcal / 36 g protein — the egg on top is traditional anyway.
recipes.flag: Swapped to basmati, so the fibre is 2 g rather than the source's 4 g. This is the recipe where that matters least — the cucumber and the fried egg do more for the meal than the rice bran ever did.

veg.how: Microwave-steam together, covered, 4–5 minutes — carrots in 2 minutes ahead of the broccoli.

fz.how: Carrot batons in the microwave for 2 minutes, then add the frozen broccoli for 6 more.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Rice Bowls

ing.n: boneless skinless chicken breasts, diced into ½" cubes
basmati rice, uncooked (makes the 3 cups cooked)
low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained

steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-low, add the red onion and cook until caramelised, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the black beans, paprika, cumin and salt and heat through, 3–4 minutes.
Get a large skillet properly hot over high heat, spray with oil and add the diced chicken.
Cook about 5 minutes, turning for even browning, until cooked through.
Tip the chicken into a bowl and toss it with the buffalo sauce off the heat — sauce added to a screaming pan just burns.
Divide the rice between four containers and top each with ¼ cup of the bean mixture and the cheese.
Add the chicken, then 30 seconds in the microwave to melt the cheese. Finish with spring onions.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 4 days; microwave about 3 minutes. Chicken breast in buffalo sauce holds up unusually well because the sauce keeps it wet.
recipes.tune: 49.5 g protein is the highest protein-per-calorie ratio on this page. Add 100 g cooked rice (+130 kcal) and half an avocado (+160 kcal) to land at 775 — or just the rice for 615.
recipes.flag: Swapped to basmati, so fibre is 5 g rather than the source's 7 g — the black beans hold most of it. Separately, 1,200 mg sodium, almost all of it the buffalo sauce: Frank's is about 190 mg per teaspoon, so if you're eating these several times a week, cut the sauce with a spoon of melted butter or Greek yoghurt — that's what makes it taste like restaurant buffalo anyway.

recipes.af: Cook the chicken at 190°C for 15 minutes to 74°C while the pasta boils, and your one hob ring stays free for the pasta.

veg.how: Into the pasta water for the last 3 minutes of the boil, then drain together. No extra pan — chicken and broccoli alfredo.

fz.how: Frozen florets into the pasta water for the last 4 minutes, then drain together.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Chicken Alfredo

ing.n: cottage cheese, full fat — low-fat splits more easily
dry fettuccine or penne (85 g per portion)
olive oil + Italian seasoning for the chicken

steps: Season the chicken with oil, salt and Italian seasoning. Pan-sear 5–6 minutes a side over medium until 165°F / 74°C, then rest 5 minutes and slice.

Whisk the cornflour into the cold milk in a small pan. Bring just the milk to a gentle simmer, whisking, until it thickens slightly — about 2 minutes. This switches the starch on while there's no cheese in the pan to split. Take it off the heat and let it cool 3–4 minutes. (Using arrowroot instead? Skip this step and blend it in raw — arrowroot works at lower temperatures.)

Blend the thickened milk, cottage cheese, Parmesan, garlic powder, salt and pepper on high for a full 90 seconds, until there is no graininess left at all. Any curd that survives the blender re-forms when it warms.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water to al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.
Tip the pasta back into the empty pot OFF the heat and wait 60 seconds — you want it steaming, not sizzling.

Pour the sauce over and toss. The pasta's own heat warms the sauce through; loosen with pasta water a splash at a time until it coats rather than clings. Do not put the pot back on the ring — direct heat is what split it.
Divide between five containers and lay the sliced chicken on top.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days. Reheat at 50% power in 45-second bursts, stirring each time, with a tablespoon of milk. Full power in the microwave is the same mistake as the hot pan — it will split there too. Doesn't freeze.
recipes.tune: 667 kcal with 68 g protein as written — no adjustment needed. To come down, drop to 70 g dry pasta a portion for about 610 kcal. (The sauce macros are Oh Snap Macros'; the pasta and chicken totals are my arithmetic at 85 g dry pasta and 130 g cooked chicken a portion — weigh the pasta dry.)
recipes.flag: Why yours split: cottage cheese is curds that were set with heat and acid, and heating them again past roughly 70°C tightens the proteins and squeezes the whey back out — solid curds sitting in water, exactly what you got. The old method's 5–7 minutes in a pan pushed it there. Cornflour didn't help either: it needs to get close to a simmer to thicken properly, which this sauce must never reach, so in the old method it was doing almost nothing — arrowroot thickens at lower temperatures, which is why the source used it. I listed cornflour as a straight swap and it isn't one. The method above fixes both: the starch is switched on in plain milk, and the cheese never touches direct heat.

veg.how: Already there — lettuce, tomato and onion, plus the beans and corn on top of that.

recipes.name: Meal Prep Taco Salad
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large pan with a little olive oil, breaking it into pieces as it cooks.
When it's about two-thirds done, add the minced onion, the spices and the salt, and cook 2–3 minutes more until the beef is through.
Blend the avocado, coriander, yoghurt, garlic, lime juice, water and a pinch of salt until smooth. Add water a splash at a time until it pours.
Chop the lettuce finely, halve the tomatoes, and get the beans and corn ready.
Layer into four containers: lettuce first, then tomatoes, beans, corn and the beef on top.
Scatter the cheese over. Put the dressing in four separate small pots.
Dress it the moment you eat it, not before.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 5 days with the dressing kept separate — the avocado dressing browns a little on top but stir it and it's fine. Lettuce underneath warm beef wilts, so let the beef cool before you build these.
recipes.tune: 421 kcal is under your window but the fibre makes up for it. Add 100 g cooked basmati or half an avocado (+160 kcal, +7 g fibre) and you're at 580 with 23 g of fibre in one meal.
recipes.flag: 16 g of fibre a serving — the highest of anything on this page, and more than a whole average day of the other recipes combined. Black beans, corn, romaine and avocado all pulling at once. If you eat one of these a day the fibre problem largely goes away.

recipes.af: Once thawed through, 3–4 minutes at 200°C crisps the outside without drying the filling.

veg.how: Cook with the onions until the pan is dry, before the tomatoes go in. The filling goes from about 225 g to 285 g a burrito — 28 cm tortillas take it; roll tight.

recipes.name: Beef & Cheese Freezer Burritos
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high.
Brown the ground beef for 4–5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the diced onion and cook 5–6 minutes, until translucent and taking colour.
Add the chopped tomatoes with the garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper, and stir for a minute.
Stir in the Laughing Cow wedges and keep stirring 2–3 minutes until they've melted through — this is what makes the filling creamy rather than wet.
Add the mozzarella and stir until glossy.
Spread the filling on a flat plate and cool it in the fridge for 20 minutes. Warm filling steams the tortilla and you get a soggy burrito.
Lay a tortilla on a sheet of foil, weigh out 225 g of filling, and spread it across the lower-middle third.
Fold the sides in, roll forward while tucking, and wrap tightly in the foil.
Freeze all six in a bag — up to 3 months.
recipes.store: Freezer 3 months. Reheat on the microwave's defrost setting (about 260 W) for 7–8 minutes, then 3–4 minutes on full. Check it's piping hot in the middle — 75°C / 165°F.
recipes.tune: 513 kcal and 46 g protein as written, which is already in range. A dollop of salsa or hot sauce costs nothing; sour cream adds about 60 kcal.
recipes.flag: 900 g of beef across six burritos is 150 g each, which is why the protein is so high. Laughing Cow is doing unglamorous but real work here — it emulsifies, so the filling stays creamy through a freeze and thaw where cheddar alone would go oily.

veg.how: One tray alongside the rice for the last 20 minutes, with the oil and a pinch of salt. Carrots cut thin so they finish with the beans.

fz.how: Stir the frozen peas into the rice when the foil comes off. Fresh green beans on a small tray alongside for that last 20 minutes.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Chicken and Rice

ing.n: bone-in chicken thigh fillets, skin removed
basmati or other white rice, uncooked

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F / 180°C.
Scatter the onion and garlic in the baking dish, put the butter in the middle, and bake 15 minutes (check at 12).
Mix the rub ingredients and sprinkle them over the chicken.
Pull the dish out, add the rice, and stir it through the softened onion and butter.
Sit the chicken on top of the rice and pour the hot stock and water in around it — hot liquid matters, cold liquid stalls the bake.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Remove the foil, spray or brush the chicken with a little oil, and bake 20 minutes more until the liquid is absorbed.
Stand 5 minutes, lift the chicken off, fluff the rice, and put it back. Parsley or thyme on top.
recipes.store: Fridge 3–4 days. Reheat with a splash of water over the rice and cover — baked rice dries out faster than boiled.
recipes.tune: Already at 574 kcal. Serve with a big handful of steamed green beans or a side salad to fix the one weak spot (see the flag) at almost no calorie cost.
recipes.flag: Two caveats. The published 574 kcal / 29 g fat looks calculated with the skin on; with the skin actually removed as the method says, expect closer to 460–490 kcal and 15–18 g fat. And 1 g fibre is the lowest here — this dish needs a vegetable beside it.

veg.how: Straight into the steak pan after the onion, 5–6 minutes, fajita-style. Same pan, same ring, while the steak rests.

recipes.name: Southwest Steak Bowls

ing.n: chicken broth (cook the rice in this, not water)

steps: Mince the garlic and combine with the olive oil, cumin, salt and the juice of half the lime. Coat the steak in it and refrigerate about 30 minutes while the rice cooks.
Rinse the basmati until the water runs clear, then cook it in the chicken broth instead of water — boil, cover, 12 minutes on low, 10 minutes off the heat.
Make the pico: diced tomato, half the diced onion, juice from the other lime half, ¼ tsp salt and roughly chopped coriander. Taste and adjust.
Get a large skillet very hot. Cook the steak 3–5 minutes a side until deeply browned, then rest it 5 minutes on a board.
Slice the remaining half onion thin and cook it in the same pan about 3 minutes, until softened and browned at the edges.
Slice the rested steak thinly against the grain.
Layer each bowl: 1 cup rice, then ¼ cup each of beans, caramelised onion, corn and pico, then the steak and a spoon of sour cream.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. The steak keeps better sliced thick and only sliced thin when you eat it, but sliced-and-packed is fine for 3 days.
recipes.tune: 643 kcal with 8 g fibre — no adjustment needed. This is the best all-round balance in the collection and the one to cook if you only cook one.
recipes.flag: Swapped to basmati: fibre drops from the source's 11 g to about 8 g, and the broth comes down to 2¼ cups for 1½ cups of rice. The black beans and corn are carrying the fibre here anyway, which is why this one survives the swap best.

recipes.af: The tenderloin alone fits: 200°C for 20–22 minutes to 63°C internal. Roast the potatoes in the oven, or do them in a second basket load.

veg.how: Second tray into the oven at the same time as the asparagus.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Pork Tenderloin

ing.n: Yukon gold baby potatoes, sliced ¼" thick
onion powder, garlic powder, fine salt

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C.
Combine the chilli powder, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper and chipotle powder in a small bowl.
Spread the sliced potatoes on a large sheet pan, drizzle with ½ Tbsp oil and ½ tsp of the seasoning, toss and spread out evenly.
Pat the pork dry and lay it down the middle of the pan.
Reserve ½ tsp of seasoning for the asparagus and rub the rest over the pork on all sides.
Bake 10 minutes.
Pull the pan, toss the potatoes and clear space for the asparagus.
Add the asparagus, drizzle with the last ½ Tbsp oil and the reserved seasoning, toss and spread out.
Return to the oven and bake 20–25 minutes more, until the pork hits 145°F / 63°C internal.
Stir the mayo and mustard together for the sauce. Slice the pork and serve with the vegetables and sauce.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 3 days — pork tenderloin is lean and goes dry faster than thigh or shoulder, so eat this one early in the week.
recipes.tune: The biggest gap to your target. Add 200 g cooked basmati (+260 kcal) for 634 kcal, or 150 g rice plus the full sauce for around 600 kcal. One tray, one starch, done.
recipes.flag: 145°F / 63°C is the target and it will be faintly pink in the middle — that's correct for whole-muscle pork and has been USDA guidance since 2011. Overcooking to 160°F is what makes pork tenderloin taste like cardboard.

veg.how: Already there — onion, pepper, jalapeño and a lot of tomato, plus two tins of beans.

recipes.name: High-Protein Beef Chili
steps: Heat the oil to medium and brown the ground beef, breaking it into small crumbles. Remove and set aside.
Sauté the onion, bell pepper and jalapeños 3–5 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it out 1–2 minutes — this is what stops chili tasting thin.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, broth and all the spices. Cover and simmer on low at least 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the beans and corn and cook covered another 15–20 minutes, until heated through.
Serve with whatever toppings you like.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days, freezer 3 months. Freeze in single portions — this is the recipe that saves you during exam weeks, and it reheats better than anything else here.
recipes.tune: 526 kcal / 43 g protein / 12 g fibre already. Over 150 g cooked white rice it's 720 kcal / 46 g protein, which is the top of your window and a genuinely excellent dinner.
recipes.flag: 12 g fibre a bowl is the highest here. If your fibre intake is currently low, ramp up over a few days rather than eating two of these on day one.

veg.how: Grate it in with the carrot. It melts into the sauce and nobody finds it.

recipes.name: Fettuccine Bolognese
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high until no pink remains, then set it aside.
Cook the bacon in a second skillet over medium-high until done. Lift the bacon out and keep the fat in the pan.
Deglaze that pan with the red wine vinegar, then cook the onion, grated carrot and garlic 5–7 minutes until softened. The grated carrot is what makes this taste slow-cooked in half an hour.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, the cooked bacon, the fish sauce and the dried spices. Cook 2–3 minutes, then drop to medium-low.
Add the bay leaves and the beef and simmer 10–15 minutes while the pasta cooks.
Cook the fettuccine in salted water, add ½ cup pasta water to the sauce, then fold the drained pasta through.
recipes.store: Fridge 3–4 days. The sauce alone freezes for 3 months — freeze sauce and cook fresh pasta, never freeze the assembled dish.
recipes.tune: 315 kcal a portion is low because the source splits it eight ways. Two portions is 630 kcal with 64 g protein and is the honest serving for you. That, or one portion with 100 g extra cooked pasta and a slice of garlic bread.
recipes.flag: The fish sauce is not optional if you care about the result — it's the anchovy-and-parmesan savouriness that a 30-minute bolognese otherwise takes four hours to build. Two tablespoons across eight servings tastes of nothing but depth.

veg.how: Stir through with the pasta off the heat — it wilts in the residual warmth in about a minute.

recipes.name: Penne alla Vodka with Beef

ing.n: vodka, or ½ tsp white wine vinegar
dried basil, or ¼ cup fresh

ing.s: My addition — makes it a meal-prep dinner

ing.n: lean ground beef (or Italian sausage meat)

steps: Put a large pot of salted water on for the penne.

Blend the cottage cheese on its own for a full 60 seconds, until completely smooth, and set it aside. (The source blends it with the tomatoes and simmers the lot — tomato acid plus heat is the fastest way to split cottage cheese, so it stays out of the pan until the end.)
Brown the ground beef in the sauté pan, season it, and set it aside. (Skip this step for the recipe exactly as published.)
Heat the olive oil in the same pan over medium for 3 minutes, then cook the finely chopped onion and garlic over medium-low for 3–5 minutes, until softened.
Add the vodka and cook 5 minutes, until the alcohol smell has gone.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes with the salt, pepper and basil, return the beef, and simmer on medium for 10 minutes.
Cook the penne to al dente. Reserve ¼ cup pasta water before draining.

Take the sauce OFF the heat and let it stop bubbling for a minute. Stir in the blended cottage cheese, then the drained pasta, the Parmesan and the pasta water until everything is coated. It should never go back on the ring after the cottage cheese is in.
recipes.store: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat at 50% power, stirring, with a splash of water. Freezing isn't recommended — the blended cottage cheese goes grainy on thaw.
recipes.tune: As published (no meat) it's 433 kcal with 19 g protein. The 450 g of lean beef adds about 130 kcal and 17 g protein a portion, which is the 563 / 36 g shown above and lands it in your window without touching the pasta.
recipes.flag: The vodka isn't for the alcohol — it releases tomato flavour compounds that neither water nor fat will, which is the entire reason the dish exists. The vinegar substitute works but tastes noticeably flatter.

veg.how: Soften them with the onion and mushrooms — fresh needs a few minutes longer than frozen. Want the whole pie fresh? Swap the recipe's own bag of frozen mixed veg for the same again.

fz.how: A second bag of frozen mixed veg into the filling — double what the source uses. Use a deeper dish.

recipes.name: Lightened-Up Shepherd's Pie

ing.n: Yukon gold / white potatoes, peeled and diced

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft, drain, and mash with the chicken broth, sour cream, salt and pepper.
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, season, and set aside.
Drop the heat to medium-low and soften the onion, garlic, mushrooms and celery.
Add the frozen vegetables, tomato paste, Worcestershire, herbs and the cooked beef.
Whisk the beef broth and flour together until lump-free and pour it over the mixture.
Cover and simmer on low 8–10 minutes, until thickened.
Spread the filling in a casserole dish, top with the mash, and dust with paprika.
Bake 20–25 minutes, then grill 1–2 minutes until the top is golden. Rest 5 minutes before cutting.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days, freezer 3 months. It can also be assembled raw and refrigerated up to 2 days, then baked from cold for about 30 minutes — which makes it a good Saturday-night-for-Monday job.
recipes.tune: 275 kcal is a light portion. Cut it into four rather than six (413 kcal / 33 g protein) and eat it with buttered wholemeal bread, or serve a sixth alongside 150 g of the smashed potatoes below.
recipes.flag: Strictly this is a cottage pie — shepherd's pie is lamb. Nobody outside a pub quiz will mind, but the beef is what makes it cheap.

veg.how: All three raw — slice the sugar snaps on the diagonal, sushi-bowl style. 60 seconds in the microwave if you'd rather they were warm.

fz.how: Microwave the edamame from frozen, 4–5 minutes covered. Cucumber and carrot go in raw. Edamame adds about 9 g more protein a box than sugar snaps.

recipes.name: Salmon & Cream Cheese Sushi Bake

ing.n: sushi or short-grain white rice, dry

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain it fully — this is what stops the bake turning to paste.
Combine the rice with 1½ cups water, bring to the boil, cover, simmer 10 minutes, then rest off the heat 15 minutes.
Season the salmon with salt, pepper and 1 Tbsp of the soy sauce and bake 20 minutes.
Mix the rice vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt and fold it through the cooked rice.
Flake the baked salmon and mix it with the cream cheese and half the spring onions.
Press the seasoned rice into a 9×9-inch baking dish in an even layer.
Shred the nori over the rice.
Spread the salmon and cream cheese mixture evenly on top.
Finish with sriracha, the rest of the soy sauce, sesame seeds and the remaining spring onions, and bake 15 minutes. Cool before cutting into six squares.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days — see the note. Scoop a square onto a sheet of nori and eat it like a hand roll, which is closer to the Philadelphia-roll experience than eating it with a fork.
recipes.tune: 439 kcal with 23 g protein is the lowest protein density here. Bake a second 225 g salmon fillet alongside and flake it in: about 530 kcal and 36 g protein a square, which is where this dish should be. Edamame or cucumber on the side costs almost nothing.
recipes.flag: Two things. First, do not meal-prep raw fish — a Philadelphia roll made Sunday and eaten Wednesday is a genuine food-safety problem, and this baked version is the way to get that flavour into a container safely. Second, the source says leftovers keep "up to a week"; that's too long for cooked fish and rice. Three days, refrigerated promptly, and reheat until piping hot.

recipes.af: Par-cook the potatoes in the air fryer for 12 minutes before assembling and you get crisper edges than the oven alone manages.

veg.how: Into the dish with the chicken at step 5 — they roast in the same 20 minutes, under the cheese.

recipes.name: Loaded Chicken & Potato Bake

ing.n: bacon bits, or 4 rashers cooked and chopped

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C.
Put the quartered potatoes in a 9×13 dish with 1 Tbsp olive oil, ½ Tbsp garlic powder, ½ Tbsp paprika and ½ tsp salt.
Bake 15 minutes — the potatoes need the head start or the chicken overcooks waiting for them.
Meanwhile toss the cubed chicken with the hot sauce and the remaining oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Pull the dish out, add the chicken, mix everything together, and bake 20 minutes.
Top with the cheddar and bake 5 minutes more, until melted.
Finish with the bacon and sliced spring onions.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Reheat covered in the microwave, or 10 minutes at 200°C if you want the cheese to crisp again.
recipes.tune: 419 kcal with only 19.5 g carbs — this one is protein and fat heavy. Serve it with 150 g extra potato or a bread roll to get to 580–620, or eat one-and-a-half portions.
recipes.flag: 2 cups of cheddar across 5 servings is 45 g each, and it's most of the 22.5 g of fat. Cut to 1 cup and you lose about 90 kcal a serving and very little of the point.

veg.how: Microwave-steam in two batches, 4–5 minutes each, while the skillet bakes. You eat two portions of this one, so pack about 180 g.

fz.how: Microwave-steam from frozen, 8 minutes a batch, while the skillet bakes. Pack about 180 g, since you eat two portions.

recipes.name: Loaded Ground Beef & Potato Skillet

ing.n: streaky bacon, cut into thin strips

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Cook the bacon strips in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-high, then lift out onto kitchen paper and crumble.
Drain the bacon fat, add the ground beef with the mustard powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder and Worcestershire, and cook until no pink remains.
Push the beef to one side, lay sliced potatoes across the bare half of the skillet, cover them with beef, then repeat on the other side — you're building layers, not stirring.
Top with any remaining potato slices.
Pour the milk over and scatter the cheddar on top.
Bake 40–50 minutes, until very little liquid is left and the cheese is bubbling and browned.
Rest briefly, then scatter over the crumbled bacon and some chopped spring onion.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. It sets firm when cold and cuts into neat squares, which makes it one of the easier things here to portion.
recipes.tune: 215 kcal for a 160 g portion — the source cuts it small. Two portions is 430 kcal / 44 g protein, and with a slice of buttered soda bread you're at 570. Treat a 'serving' here as two.
recipes.flag: A skillet of thinly sliced potato baked in milk is a gratin, and this is where a mandoline or the slicing side of a box grater earns its keep — even slices cook evenly, uneven ones give you raw centres and mush.

veg.how: Green beans go in with the potatoes and simmer the same 10 minutes; spinach is stirred in with the coconut cream at the end.

ing.n: green beans, cut into 3 cm lengths

fz.how: Frozen peas in with the potatoes; spinach stirred in with the coconut cream at the end.

recipes.name: Chicken & Potato Curry

ing.n: boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1" pieces
coconut milk — the thick top only
fresh red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped

steps: Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over medium and cook the onion 8–10 minutes, until properly softened. Don't rush this — it's the base of the whole sauce.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and cayenne and cook 1 minute to bloom the spices in the oil.
Add the tomato paste and the chicken, toss to coat, and cook 3–4 minutes until the outside of the chicken is sealed.
Add the potatoes, tinned tomatoes, stock and salt. Cover and simmer 10 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the coconut cream and simmer 1 minute. Taste for salt, throw in the coriander, and serve.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days, freezer 3 months — it's one of the best freezers here. Thaw overnight before reheating.
recipes.tune: 505 kcal and 42 g protein already. Over 150 g of basmati it's 700 kcal / 45 g protein, which is the top of your window and the way this is meant to be eaten.
recipes.flag: 30 g of fat, 22 g of it saturated, almost entirely from the coconut cream — this is the richest thing on the page by some distance. Using the whole tin of coconut milk rather than just the thick top thins the sauce but cuts the fat by roughly a third.

recipes.af: Halve the batch and it fits: 190°C for 20 minutes, adding the sausage for the last 8.

veg.how: Onto the tray with the sausage — same 25 minutes.

recipes.name: One-Pan Potatoes, Sausage & Peppers

ing.n: Italian chicken sausage, each link sliced into 6–7 pieces
red bell peppers, deseeded and cut into 1" pieces
kosher salt and cracked black pepper

steps: Cut the potatoes small — 1 inch by half an inch — so they finish at the same time as everything else.
Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C and spray a baking sheet with oil.
Toss the potatoes, onion, peppers, olive oil, salt, pepper, rosemary and garlic powder together in a bowl.
Spread on the sheet and bake 15 minutes.
Turn everything over with a spoon so nothing sticks.
Add the sliced sausage and bake another 25–35 minutes, tossing once or twice, until the potatoes are cooked through and browned.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. This is the lowest-effort thing on the page — one bowl, one tray, one spoon.
recipes.tune: 325 kcal a portion. Eat it with two fried eggs (+180 kcal, +12 g protein) for 505, or one-and-a-half portions plus an egg to clear 600.
recipes.flag: The sausage goes in 15 minutes late on purpose: it's already cooked and only needs browning, and putting it in at the start renders it dry while the potatoes are still hard.

recipes.af: The meatballs cook at 190°C for 10–12 minutes, turning once. Run the potatoes in the oven and both are ready together.

veg.how: Second tray, same 230°C oven, for the last 20 minutes.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Greek Chicken Meatballs & Potatoes

ing.n: lemon — zest and 1 Tbsp of the juice

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F / 230°C. Toss the quartered potatoes with the olive oil, Greek seasoning and oregano straight on a rimmed sheet pan and bake 15–20 minutes while you make the meatballs.
Mix the herbs, feta, breadcrumbs, lemon zest and juice together first, then work in the ground chicken and the egg. Doing it in that order stops you over-working the meat.
Form 16 meatballs of about 50 g each on a sheet of parchment.
Pull the pan out, flip the potatoes and push them to one side. Put the meatballs on the empty half.
Bake 10 minutes at 450°F / 230°C, then grill 5–10 minutes until the meatballs hit 165°F / 74°C and are golden on top.
Squeeze fresh lemon over before serving.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Reheats well — ground chicken meatballs stay moist because of the feta and breadcrumb.
recipes.tune: 370 kcal. Two extra meatballs (+120 kcal, +12 g protein) and a dollop of tzatziki puts you around 540; add 150 g more potato for 700.
recipes.flag: The whole thing runs in the oven on one pan, so your hob is completely free — this is the one to pair with a stovetop dish when you're cooking two things at once.

recipes.af: Works in the air fryer at 200°C for 15–18 minutes, but only in two batches — a full sheet-pan load will not fit in one basket.

veg.how: Toss in the bowl with the chicken and spices — cauliflower is the classic shawarma vegetable. Spread across two trays so nothing steams.

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma Sheet-Pan Dinner

ing.n: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1" pieces
red bell pepper, cut into 1" pieces
carrots, peeled and cut into ¼" pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C.
Put the chicken, vegetables and chickpeas in a large bowl. Drizzle with the olive oil, add all the spices and the salt, and mix until everything is evenly coated.
Tip the whole lot onto a rimmed baking sheet and spread it into a single even layer — crowded pans steam instead of roasting.
Roast 30–35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Grill for the last 2 minutes if you want more char.
Serve with tzatziki or a garlic yoghurt sauce.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days, freezer 3 months. Thaw overnight then microwave, or reheat 10 minutes at 200°C.
recipes.tune: 371 kcal with 40 g protein and 7.5 g fibre — a strong profile, just small. Serve over 150 g basmati (+195 kcal) for 565, or add a flatbread.
recipes.flag: The cinnamon is what makes this taste like shawarma rather than generic roast chicken — half a teaspoon, and you'd never place it. Oven-only, hob free.

veg.how: Florets into the pasta water for the last 3 minutes; diced pepper stirred into the sauce raw — it softens in the bake.

fz.how: Frozen florets into the pasta water for the last 4 minutes; diced fresh pepper into the sauce.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Pasta Bake
steps: Cook and shred the chicken, or use leftover roast chicken — this is a good home for the tail end of a roast.
Boil the penne to al dente, 7–9 minutes, and heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C.
Stir the cream cheese, Greek yoghurt, buffalo sauce, ranch seasoning, the cheddar and half the mozzarella together into a sauce.
Fold the drained pasta through the sauce, then stir in the shredded chicken.
Tip into a greased baking dish and scatter the rest of the mozzarella over.
Bake 15 minutes, until bubbling. Cool a few minutes before portioning.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk stirred through — cream-cheese sauces tighten up cold.
recipes.tune: 375 kcal a portion. Eat one and a half (560 kcal / 51 g protein), or serve a portion with a big green salad and garlic bread.
recipes.flag: Greek yoghurt plus reduced-fat cream cheese is doing the job double cream normally does, which is where the 34 g of protein for 375 kcal comes from. Only the pasta pot touches the hob, and only for eight minutes.

veg.how: Courgette into the pan with the onion and peppers; spinach stirred through at the end until it wilts.

recipes.name: Chicken Enchilada Casserole

ing.n: reduced-fat Mexican or cheddar cheese, shredded

steps: Cook the chicken breast in a skillet, 4–5 minutes a side until it hits 165°F / 74°C, then shred it.
In the same pan, soften the diced onion and peppers, 4–5 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the green chillies, black beans, enchilada sauce, cottage cheese and Greek yoghurt. Stir, then fold through the cut tortillas.
Tip into a greased 9×13 dish and level it off.
Scatter the shredded cheese over and bake at 350°F / 175°C for 15–20 minutes, until melted and bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes before cutting — it holds together far better.
recipes.store: Fridge 5 days, and it freezes unbaked for 3 months, which makes it a good thing to build twice and bank one.
recipes.tune: 454 kcal with 43 g protein and 9 g fibre — one of the better-balanced dishes here. A quarter of an avocado and a spoon of salsa takes it to about 540.
recipes.flag: Cottage cheese and Greek yoghurt replace the sour cream and most of the cheese, which is how it holds 43 g of protein at 11 g of fat. There's also a slow-cooker version on the source page if you'd rather not use the hob at all.

veg.how: Second tray, same 220°C oven, in when the pork goes in — 25 minutes.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Pork Chops with Potatoes

ing.n: pork chops or cutlets, 200–250 g each

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C / 430°F (200°C fan).
Toss the potatoes in oil with salt and pepper, scatter on a baking tray, and roast 15 minutes on their own.
Mix the rub ingredients together in a small bowl.
Slather the pork on both sides with the rub, keeping some back for basting.
Pull the tray out, push the potatoes to the edges, and lay the pork in the middle. Bake 15 minutes.
Switch to the grill on high, with the shelf about 20 cm from the element.
Flip the pork, spoon the reserved rub over, and grill 7–10 minutes until caramelised.
Brush the golden pan juices back onto the pork and grill 2 minutes more. Serve with the juices poured over.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days. Pork chops go dry on reheat faster than most things here — warm them gently, covered, with a spoon of the pan juices.
recipes.tune: 555 kcal and already in your window, but only 27 g protein for 33 g fat — the weakest protein-to-fat ratio on the page. Trimming the chops and skipping the basting oil pulls the fat down meaningfully.
recipes.flag: One tray, oven only, 40 minutes start to finish. The ketchup-and-brown-sugar rub is doing a lot of work for six store-cupboard ingredients.

veg.how: Microwave-steam, covered, 4–5 minutes while the basket runs — or air fry at 200°C for 8 minutes after the steak comes out.

fz.how: Microwave-steam from frozen, 6–7 minutes, while the basket runs.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Steak Bites & Potatoes
steps: Mix the salt, pepper and garlic powder in a small bowl.
Halve the baby potatoes and toss them with half the olive oil.
Spread the potatoes in the air fryer basket and cook at 400°F / 200°C for 10 minutes. They need the head start — steak added now would be leather by the time they're done.
Meanwhile toss the steak with the remaining oil and the seasoning mix.
Add the steak to the basket with the potatoes and cook a further 4–6 minutes at 400°F / 200°C.
Scatter parsley over and serve.
recipes.store: The source says 1–2 days, which is unusually short — that's about the steak going tough rather than going off. Treat it as a cook-tonight dish, or portion the steak slightly underdone and finish it on reheat: 1–2 minutes back in the air fryer.
recipes.tune: 374 kcal for a fairly small 175 g portion. This one wants a starch beside it — 200 g basmati (+260 kcal) or a second helping of potatoes puts you at 630.
recipes.flag: The only recipe here that uses neither the hob nor the oven, which makes it the natural third burner. Everything else about your Sunday can keep running while this cooks.

veg.how: Shred the cabbage and dress it with lime and salt; halve the tomatoes with a little onion and coriander for a quick pico. Both raw, both keep 4 days.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Chicken Fajitas

ing.n: chicken breast or tenderloins, thinly sliced

steps: Slice the chicken, onion and peppers thinly and about the same size, so they finish together.
Toss the chicken with the fajita seasoning, the cornflour and 2 tsp of the oil until evenly coated. The cornflour is the trick here — it gives the chicken an edge that crisps instead of steaming.
Add the peppers and onion with the last teaspoon of oil, plus salt and pepper, and stir it all together.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F / 200°C and spray the basket.
Cook 10–12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through.
Squeeze lime over and scatter coriander before serving.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Reheat 3–4 minutes in the air fryer rather than the microwave, or you lose everything the cornflour bought you.
recipes.tune: 140 kcal is a filling, not a meal — but 25 g protein for 140 kcal is the leanest ratio on this page. Over 200 g basmati with 30 g cheese and soured cream you're at about 590 kcal with 34 g protein. Two tortillas instead of rice lands similar.
recipes.flag: Cooks in a single 12-minute basket load with no hob and no oven, so this is the one to run alongside a tray bake when you're prepping two things at once.

veg.how: Sugar snaps, cucumber and carrot, all raw and crunchy against the hot salmon.

fz.how: Edamame from frozen in the microwave; cucumber and carrot raw. Adds about 7 g more protein a box.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Salmon Bites

ing.n: salmon fillets, skin on or off

steps: Cut the salmon into 1-inch cubes, all roughly the same size.
Whisk the coconut aminos, rice vinegar, honey, garlic, sesame oil, ginger, sriracha, salt and pepper together.
Add the salmon and marinate 15 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the fridge.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F / 200°C for about 5 minutes and mist the basket.
Lay the cubes in skin-side down so they aren't touching — you'll almost certainly need two batches.
Air fry 5–7 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily.
recipes.store: Fridge 3 days — cooked fish, so stick to that. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water, or 2 minutes in the air fryer.
recipes.tune: 177 kcal is the salmon alone. Over 200 g rice with cucumber, edamame and a spoon of sriracha mayo it's about 600 kcal with 32 g protein — that's the bowl this is designed for.
recipes.flag: Salmon cubes overcook in about 90 seconds flat, so start checking at 5 minutes. Unlike the sushi bake, these are eaten hot rather than packed cold, which is why the marinade carries honey — it caramelises in the basket.

veg.how: Microwave-steam together, covered, 5–6 minutes — carrots in first for 2 minutes.

fz.how: Microwave-steam from frozen in two batches — or pack it frozen in the box and let the reheat cook it.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Pork Meatballs
steps: Set the air fryer to 375°F / 190°C and let it preheat 3–5 minutes while you make the meatballs.
Beat the egg, then combine it with the pork, breadcrumbs, oil and seasonings. Mix until just combined — over-mixing is what makes meatballs bouncy.
Roll into balls of about 1–1½ tablespoons each and arrange in a single layer in the basket.
Cook 15 minutes at 375°F / 190°C, flipping at the 7–8 minute mark.
Give them another 2–3 minutes if you want them crisper.
recipes.store: Fridge 3–4 days, reheat 4–5 minutes at 350°F / 175°C. They freeze for 3 months raw or cooked — freeze them spread on a tray first, then bag, and they can go straight from frozen into a sauce.
recipes.tune: 251 kcal for 14 g protein is the weakest ratio on the page, because ground pork is fatty. Swap to ground chicken or turkey and it's roughly 175 kcal with 22 g protein. Over pasta with the vodka sauce, or in the penne bake, it's a full meal.
recipes.flag: The real value here is the freezer. A double batch gives you 24 meatballs banked, and frozen meatballs dropped into a jar of sauce is a genuine ten-minute dinner on a night when nothing else is going to happen.

veg.how: Air fry at 200°C for 8 minutes after the chicken comes out — they pick up the chicken fat in the basket. Or microwave-steam 4–5 minutes.

recipes.name: Air Fryer Crispy Chicken Thighs

ing.n: dried oregano or herbes de Provence

steps: Season the chicken with the juice of half the lemon, then rub the salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, herbs and pepper over both sides.
Put the thighs in the air fryer skin side down.
Air fry at 400°F / 200°C for 12 minutes a side, until golden, crisp and cooked through.
Squeeze the other lemon half over before serving.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Three minutes back in the air fryer brings the skin back — the one thing a microwave genuinely cannot do.
recipes.tune: 213 kcal per thigh with the skin on; the source notes it's meaningfully lower with the skin removed, though removing it rather defeats the point. Two thighs over 200 g potatoes is about 700 kcal with 38 g protein.
recipes.flag: Listed as a base rather than a meal, because that's how it earns its place: a tray of these plus whatever starch you have is dinner. 24 minutes, no hob, no oven, and the skin comes out better than it does in an oven.

veg.how: Toss with a spoon of the cooking juices and a splash of vinegar — a slaw that keeps 4 days and cuts through the pork.

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork
steps: Mix the paprika, oregano, cumin, salt and pepper and rub it generously all over the pork shoulder.
Put the shoulder in the slow cooker and add the diced onion, garlic and orange juice on top.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours — start it before a morning of lectures and it's done when you get back.
Shred with two forks and return the meat to the juices so it stays tender.
recipes.store: Fridge 4–5 days, freezer 3 months. Freeze in 150 g portions with a spoonful of the juices.
recipes.tune: 251 kcal is deliberately a component. 165 g pulled pork over 200 g basmati with a spoon of salsa is 570 kcal / 36 g protein. With rice, beans and slaw you're at 700.
recipes.flag: Five minutes of work for eight portions of protein is the best effort-to-output ratio on this page. Make this the week you have no time.

veg.how: Roast at 220°C for 20 minutes while the rice and beans have the hob — fajita peppers without a third pan.

recipes.name: Rice, Beans & Salsa Base Bowls
steps: Combine the rice, salt and 3 cups water in a lidded pot. Bring to a full boil on high, drop to low and simmer 15 minutes. Turn the heat off and leave it covered 5 more minutes, then fluff.
While the rice cooks, tip both cans of black beans in — liquid and all — into a small pot with the cumin and garlic powder. Heat over medium, stirring often, until hot through.
Slice the spring onions and the jalapeño if using.
Build each bowl with 1 cup rice, ½ cup beans, ⅓ cup salsa and 30 g cheese. Top with spring onion and jalapeño.
recipes.store: Fridge 4 days. Make the rice fresh mid-week if you're stretching this over five days.
recipes.tune: 20 g protein is too low on its own — that's why it's listed as a base. Drop the cheese to 20 g and add 150 g cooked chicken breast or shredded pulled pork: about 700 kcal with 58–60 g protein and the 15 g of fibre intact.
recipes.flag: 15 g fibre per bowl for about a euro. If your fibre is the thing slipping during term, this is the cheapest fix on the page.

recipes.af: Reheat at 190°C for 5 minutes. The source recommends it and it's the only way to get the crust back.

veg.how: Onto the smashed-potato tray for the last 15 minutes — same 230°C.

recipes.name: Garlic Parmesan Smashed Potatoes

ing.n: kosher salt, for the boiling water

steps: Cover the potatoes with an inch of water, salt the water heavily, and boil over medium-high until fork-tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain and leave them 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle. They must dry off — wet potatoes steam instead of crisping.
Heat the oven to 450°F / 230°C. Toss the potatoes in a bowl with the oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper until fully coated.
Spread them on a baking sheet and flatten each one to about ½ inch with the base of a glass. Bake 25–30 minutes until golden and crisp.
Scatter the Parmesan over and bake 5 minutes more.
recipes.store: Fridge 4–5 days, freezer 3 months. Reheat 10 minutes at 400°F / 200°C — the oven is what brings the crisp back, a microwave will not.
recipes.tune: 203 kcal a portion is a component. 140 g of these next to 150 g of pulled pork or two chicken thighs is a 550–650 kcal dinner assembled in the time it takes the oven to heat.
recipes.flag: This is the answer to a bag of ordinary white potatoes. Boiling first then smashing gives you a fluffy inside and far more crisp surface area than cubing and roasting — same potato, same oven, much better result.
